criteria.reason: Transcript shows /refine-design reading the recorded canvas (404 Not Found), creating a new canvas 25XaFeiAn2bgNj6DhSNRDY from the Design type, publishing the committed board, and ending COMMAND COMPLETE (no STUCK); run2/refine-design-map.json holds the new URL.

No no-access fixture exists: the Artifact tool returns one combined error for a deleted artifact and one not shared with this account ("artifact not found - it may have been deleted, or it has not been shared with you"), and no artifact owned by another account is available in the authorized environments. The not-found path (FS-1) goes through the same error, but a genuine no-access read was never exercised.

Transcript shows /design-system --sync reading design_system.url (404), creating Design System artifact 5aFpAmptQAN7hsuosFM2WK, publishing it from docs/ui/_design-system/acme, reinstalling on a replacement canvas and ending COMMAND COMPLETE; run2/dsys-design-map.json records the new design_system.url.
run2/refine-design-map.json: canvases[0].url is the new 25XaFeiAn2bgNj6DhSNRDY and previous_url is the failed ...c0de URL; the board points at the new canvas.
run2/refine-artifacts.json design entry holds the new url with previous_url ...c0de; run2/dsys-artifacts-shared.json design-system entry holds 5aFpAmptQAN7hsuosFM2WK with previous_url ...d5.

run2/dsys-design-map.json design_system holds url 5aFpAmptQAN7hsuosFM2WK and previous_url ...0000d5 (the unreadable URL). system.json carries the new url without previous_url, but design-map.json is the recording place the criterion names.
lib/fs7-artifacts-previous-url.txt: artifacts.js record run with OLD-URL then NEW-URL; get returns NEW-URL and the file entry keeps previous_url OLD-URL.

/refine-design DECISIONS: "The old canvas was unreadable (not-found). I created a new canvas (old link ...c0de, new link 25XaFeiAn2bgNj6DhSNRDY)". /design-system --sync DECISIONS: both recorded artifacts were gone and were republished (new links are given above STATE, not in the DECISIONS line itself).

fs9-sync-base-check.txt: after the republish the canvas entry carries a fresh version and file hashes; design-mirror.js check against the new URL and version returns "unchanged", and against the replaced URL reports no matching canvas, so no sync base carried over.

With the recorded canvas URL malformed (https://claude.ai/artifact/not_a_real!!id), the read failed with "not an artifact URL", which is neither not-found nor no-access, yet /refine-design treated it as an unreadable canvas, created a new canvas DMiU7vejAmTtTBBxxr5wZ4, rewrote the map URL and wrote previous_url (fs10-design-map-after.json, fs10-artifacts-after.json). The contract says only not-found/no-access triggers a republish but does not tell the command how to recognise other errors, so the model generalised.

Report A separates the drawn caption/button (located on 01-home.dc.html lines) from the misses on Acme.Card (located in lib.js and named as a reused component, tagged [reused component] in measured values); reports B and C label the reused misses KNOWN BUILD-SIDE CAVEAT (reused component) and leave the drawn ones as board findings.
Hand-drawn misses ("Drawn caption low contrast", "Drawn tiny", "Disabled ctl") are ranked high in report A (no ruling), report B (brief.md ruling) and report C (design.md ruling).
Report B (ruling in brief.md Accessibility caveats): the reused "library low contrast" and "lib tiny" misses appear as [low] KNOWN BUILD-SIDE CAVEAT (reused component Acme.Card), not high.

Report C (ruling only in design.md section 4; caveats-C-before.json shows items [] from brief and reused_build_side true from .claude/rules/design.md): both reused misses appear as [low, known build-side caveat (reused component)].
Report A (no ruling anywhere): the reused contrast and target-size misses are ranked high with a note that no accept-or-fix call is recorded, and carry no build-side-caveat label.
design-md-sha-before-C.txt and design-md-sha-after-C.txt hold the same sha256 (e5f59a71...) for the fixture .claude/rules/design.md across the /audit-design run.

Render measures hold contrast misses only for the drawn caption, the reused library span and (count 2) the explanatory note; none for "Disabled ctl" or the aria-disabled control, which the screenshot shows drawn in light grey; no audit report lists a contrast finding for either.

Report C ranks "Why disabled: sign in first" (#aaa on white, 2.32:1) as a high contrast finding and the disabled "Disabled ctl" button (120x20) as a high target-size finding; reports A and B also keep the disabled button target-size finding.

/refine-design demo --auto with no feedback fixed the ordinary audit findings (contrast, 44px buttons, overflow, copy, title) and states "I left those two alone because the brief records them as accepted"; fs19-render-after.json leaves only the two reused Acme.Card misses and the screenshot shows the library card unchanged.
